title: Rusyns
summary: Rusyns, also referred to as Carpatho-Rusyns or Ruthenians, are an East Slavic ethnic group primarily located in the Eastern Carpathians, with a significant presence in Ukraine. They speak the Rusyn language, which is debated as either a separate language or a dialect of Ukrainian, and have a unique cultural identity recognized in several Central and Eastern European countries.

sections.heading: Ethnic Identity and Recognition
paragraphs: Rusyns, known by various names including Carpatho-Rusyns, Carpatho-Russians, and Rusnaks, primarily identify as a distinct ethnic group. They are recognized as such in countries like Croatia, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Serbia, and Slovakia, where they hold official minority status. However, in [[ukraine|Ukraine]], they are classified as a subgroup of [[ukrainians|Ukrainians]].

sections.heading: Language and Religion
paragraphs: The Rusyn language is an East Slavic variety that is sometimes considered a separate language and at other times viewed as a dialect of [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]]. The majority of Rusyns practice Eastern Catholicism, while a minority adhere to Eastern Orthodoxy.

sections.heading: Historical Origins
paragraphs: The origins of the Rusyn people are complex, with theories suggesting descent from early Slavic populations influenced by various migrations and invasions. The region of the Eastern [[carpathians|Carpathians]] has been populated by different tribes, including the White Croats and other East Slavic groups, contributing to the formation of the modern Rusyn identity.

sections.heading: Anthropological and Genetic Studies
paragraphs: Anthropological research indicates that the Eastern Carpathian population represents a sub-regional group within the broader Ukrainian population. Genetic studies have shown that Rusyns share common ancestry with other European populations, with specific Y-DNA studies revealing their close genetic ties to Ukrainians and Slovaks.

sections.heading: Cultural Revival
paragraphs: Since the Revolutions of 1989, there has been a resurgence in Rusyn cultural identity, particularly in regions where they reside. This revival has led to increased recognition and a reaffirmation of their distinct heritage within the context of Ukraine and neighboring countries.
